candidates.change_summary: Remove the require guard so anyone can call withdraw, changing who receives the contract balance.
Change the recipient of the transfer from Owner to msg.sender so the caller receives the contract balance.
Transfer only half the contract balance to Owner instead of the full balance.
Make the function non-payable (remove payable) so calls with value revert, changing observable behavior after withdraw.
Add a require that msg.sender is not the Owner, so Owner cannot withdraw and behavior differs.

Replace the low-level call without checking its return value with a call that requires success (reverts on failure), changing whether the Command call can silently fail and thus altering post-call observable state.
Change the call to use a staticcall (disallowing state writes) so behavior of Command differs when target requires state changes.
Move the value forwarding to zero (drop msg.value) so the call no longer forwards ETH, changing observable balances after Command.
Invert the ownership check so only non-owners can execute Command, changing which caller can invoke it and thus observable behavior.
Add a transfer of the contract balance to Owner before executing the call, altering balances observable after Command.
Change the transfer amount to send only the contract's current balance (omit adding msg.value), altering final sent value and thus observable balance after multiplicate.
Change the condition to require msg.value strictly greater than the contract balance, changing whether transfer executes and thus observable state.
Invert the branch condition so transfer happens when msg.value is less than the contract balance, changing when funds are moved and affecting observable balance.
Remove the require check inside the branch (delete the require statement), allowing transfer even if overflow-like condition would have prevented it, changing observable behavior.
Replace the transfer with a call to send one wei less than the sum, altering final transferred amount and observable balance.
